case: Berlin preliminary investigation into suspected incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung, section 130 of the German Criminal Code) over the '50 holocausts' remark
description: At a joint press conference with Chancellor Olaf Scholz at the Chancellery in Berlin on 16 August 2022, Abbas was asked whether he would apologise for the killing of Israeli athletes by the Black September group at the 1972 Munich Olympics. He replied: 'If we want to go over the past, go ahead. I have 50 slaughters that Israel committed in 50 Palestinian villages… 50 massacres, 50 slaughters, 50 holocausts.' After a criminal complaint accusing him of relativising the Holocaust, Berlin police opened a preliminary investigation for incitement to hatred under section 130 of the Criminal Code, which bars downplaying Nazi crimes; findings were to go to the Berlin public prosecutor. The police noted that a preliminary inquiry does not automatically entail a full investigation, and the German Foreign Ministry said that, as a representative of the Palestinian Authority visiting in an official capacity, he would enjoy immunity from prosecution. Scholz said he was 'disgusted' by the remarks. Abbas issued a statement walking back his remarks and describing the Holocaust as 'the most heinous crime in modern history'.
outcome: In November 2022 the Berlin public prosecutor's office closed the preliminary investigation. In a letter to Bild it said there were not 'sufficient indications' that the remarks amounted to incitement to hatred under section 130, describing his aim as highlighting what he considers crimes by the Israeli army 'while attempting to make an extremely inappropriate historical comparison'. A further complaint referred the matter to the attorney general's office; a German official told The Times of Israel the decision was unlikely to be overturned, noting his diplomatic immunity. No later reopening was found as of October 2026. The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the closure.
court: Berlin Police and Public Prosecutor's Office (Staatsanwaltschaft Berlin), Germany
presumption_note: The investigation was closed at the preliminary stage without charges; Abbas was never charged or tried and is presumed innocent.
key_facts: 16 August 2022: '50 holocausts' remark at a press conference with Olaf Scholz, who later condemned it
August 2022: Berlin police open a preliminary investigation for suspected incitement to hatred after a complaint
German Foreign Ministry: Abbas enjoyed immunity as an official visitor
November 2022: prosecutors close the case, finding insufficient indications of an offence under section 130
